purpose: PHASE 69. Every attack class the manifest names, mapped to the test that covers it or to the reason none does. Checked by scripts/orion_v2_attack_check.py, which fails when a class has neither — so a deleted security test is a failing build rather than a quiet loss of coverage.
note: A `test` entry is matched against the literal `it("...")` title in the file. Renaming a test without updating this file fails the check, which is the intent: the mapping is only worth having if it cannot silently go stale.

tests.title: rejects an action sourced only from quoted untrusted content
does not let untrusted text trigger a Tier 1 real action
ignores a model-forged trusted_user tag and fails closed
still refuses a target that only ever appeared in content Orion read
lets Nick approve out loud, and refuses the same words from a page

classes.note: The second is the newest and the sharpest: a page saying the exact approval phrase, arriving as a forged trusted_user instruction, must not open a gate.

tests.title: authorizes from the real user turn and derives every hash server-side
requires a real user turn to change Orion's own permission profile
does not open for a hash alone, only for a grant
holds the three things no delegation may cover
never lets a mode reach something the profile did not grant
lets Nick grant a capability when he names it and asks for it

classes.note: The authority floor is the load-bearing one: a mode that could relax an authority change would let Orion relax it.

tests.title: spends a grant exactly once
lets an approval go stale rather than waiting forever
consumes a tool-call binding exactly once
derives hashes for a plain append and never double-appends on retry
binds destructive approval to canonical action and context
will not let an approval be reused for a different change
ignores a grant whose nonce was not the one minted
rejects marker traversal and never creates an escaped path
blocks Desktop traversal, hidden/sensitive paths, and symlink following
rejects scratch traversal and untrusted scratch creation
names repositories by key, and a path is not a key
builds a fixed argv that no argument can extend
only lets an automation run something from the closed table
refuses a raw cron string, because a minute field is a factor of sixty

classes.note: No shell is used anywhere in the execution path; every spawn passes argv directly. The tests assert the argv cannot be extended rather than that quoting works.

tests.title: builds the environment from an allowlist, so a new secret is absent by default
does not allow an underspecified email send

classes.note: Also enforced outside the plugin: orion_v2_secret_scan.py in CI, FORBIDDEN_CONFIG on credential-shaped keys, and the credential-shape refusals in orion-remember, orion-note, orion-skill and orion-messages-send.

tests.title: reads task status past a corrupt ledger line

classes.note: The ledger is JSONL and every record is JSON.stringify'd, so a newline in a value cannot forge a record. orion-remote strips control characters from inbound text before it reaches the audit line. Partial: there is no test that specifically feeds a newline through to a ledger write.

classes.reason: The only SQL in the system is the Messages read, and it opens chat.db with mode=ro&immutable=1 and uses parameterised queries with a bounded integer limit. There is no user-supplied SQL anywhere, and no database this system writes to.
classes.residual: If a future action ever composes SQL from an argument, this becomes a real class and needs a test the same day.

classes.reason: There is no fetch primitive Orion can point at a URL. Browser control opens a tab via `open -b` at http/https only; weather calls one keyless endpoint with a place name. Nothing takes a URL and returns its body to the model.
classes.residual: browser_open_url is checked against untrusted data carriage (urlCarriesUntrustedData) but the tab's CONTENT is read by a separate, gated action. A real fetch primitive would make this class live.

classes.reason: Single user, single tenant. There are no object ids scoped to a user, no multi-user records, and no API that takes an id belonging to somebody else. The approval ticket is the closest thing to an opaque id, and it is bound to a device and a nonce.
classes.residual: Phase 83 is Multi-User Hardening. This class becomes live the moment a second identity exists, and the ticket/grant design is where it would be tested first.

classes.reason: Same as BOLA: one user. The nearest real exposure is other people's words in Nick's iMessage history, which is why messages_read is its own tier with its own flag rather than folded into home_read.

There are no sessions to steal in the web sense — no cookies, no bearer tokens issued by this system, no listening socket that accepts credentials. The Discord bridge authenticates outbound only, and the gateway binds locally.
classes.residual: The bridge's bot token IS a stealable credential, and it lives in a 0600 .env with only two values copied out of the repo's .env. Rotation is manual.

classes.reason: OAuth refresh tokens for Gmail live in the macOS Keychain, bound to the app's designated requirement — which is exactly what orion-identity-check exists to protect, since a resigned build reads as a different app and cannot decrypt them.
classes.residual: No test asserts the tokens are unreadable by another process; that is a macOS guarantee this system relies on rather than one it enforces.

classes.reason: Nothing listens for a webhook. The Discord webhook is OUTBOUND only, and the gateway exposes no inbound HTTP endpoint.
classes.residual: Phase 68's 'duplicate webhooks' and 'missing webhooks' become live if an inbound endpoint is ever added.

classes.reason: Orion does not open attachments. Gmail reads are text-only through orion-gmail-search/latest with --readonly and --gmail-no-send hard-wired, and no action downloads or opens a file from a message.
classes.residual: Any future attachment handling starts as an untrusted observation, but nothing tests that today because nothing does it.

tests.title: builds a fixed argv that no argument can extend

classes.note: The relevant assertion is that package_install is `npm ci` and never `npm install <name>` — it can only install the committed lockfile. `npm audit` runs in CI, reported rather than fatal. The honest residual is large: `npm ci` still runs install scripts, and tests_run/build_run execute repository code.
